correctness.rationale: Two full-domain exact-integer implementations enumerated all 32,768 pinned states and all 65,536 ordinary states, using independent update and digraph methods. Both agree exactly on the 425 fixed and 301 two-cycle orbits, 11 populated depth-period cells totaling 32,768, 24 states at sharp depth six, witness path 35537 -> 35025 -> 32977 -> 209 -> 81 -> 17 -> 1, pinned all-one basin 9,383, single-positive basin 3,696, ordinary all-one basin 8,229, and gain/loss counts 1,154/0. The local rule is monotone and pinning coordinatewise increases its output, proving no loss analytically. Programs were replayed from current exact source files before packaging. Finite exhaustive classification is not extrapolated to higher dimensions.

value.rationale: The intervention is natural: a single immutable opinion on a vertex-transitive, even-degree sixteen-vertex communication network, keeping the original majority rule elsewhere. The exact matched-input gain 1,154 with zero losses coexists with a sharp increase of the settling time four to six and a 3,696-state polarized basin. These mutually contrasting dynamical outcomes and a complete finite orbit/entry classification create a meaningful calibrated benchmark, not merely a textbook corollary or arbitrary parameter choice.
